additions.label: prop:arith-denominator
additions.topic: Explicit universal denominator product and clearing identity
additions.hypotheses: N >= 1, 0 <= j < N, n natural. Lean also allows the recurrence parameters outside this original-family domain.
additions.mathematics: D_(N,j)(n) = product_(r=1)^n binom(N*r+j,N*r); D_(N,j)(n) C_(N,j)(n) is an integer, including n=0.
additions.proof_in_manuscript: Induction through the triangular recurrence and divisibility among the products.

additions.label: ex:arith-bernoulli

supporting_sources.location: Example 3.5; Euler boundary immediately preceding in Example 3.4 is already present in the consolidated section.

additions.proof_in_manuscript: Common-denominator identity and comparison of even formal-series coefficients.
additions.formalization_limit: No dedicated packet-to-Bernoulli Lean theorem was matched; no new formal verification is claimed.

additions.label: prop:arith-lucas-window
additions.topic: Lucas row reduction, integral coefficients, and common reduction for addresses below p
additions.hypotheses: p prime, m > 0, j < p and k < p where k is used; n,q natural. No m | p-1 hypothesis is required.
additions.mathematics: binom(m*p*n+j,m*p*q) = binom(m*n,m*q) modulo p; normalized coefficients are p-adically integral and all these addresses share the unique reduced triangular inverse.
additions.proof_in_manuscript: Lucas low digit separation, unit diagonal recurrence over Z_p, and uniqueness after reduction to F_p.

additions.label: eq:arith-signed-zigzag
additions.topic: Original signed zigzag expression for the odd-length inverse coefficients
additions.hypotheses: m natural; Z_r defined by sec(t)+tan(t), gamma_m by the already retained sech(t)^2 expansion.
additions.proof_in_manuscript: Differentiate tan(t), use parity of sec(t), and change the sign in the squared formal variable.
additions.formalization_limit: The generating-function convention is matched; the alternating-permutation counting interpretation is not claimed.

additions.label: ex:arith-normalization-loss
additions.topic: Exact counterexample showing the factorial correction is necessary
additions.hypotheses: p=3, m=2, N=6, j=3, n=1, h=1, order one.
additions.mathematics: C_(6,3)(1)=-1/84, C_(6,3)(2)=703/5460, difference=64/455, valuation at 3 is 0. Unnormalized difference=384/455 has valuation 1.
additions.proof_in_manuscript: The exact recurrence evaluations and prime valuations exhibit failure of a bound without factorial loss within the claimed parameter range.

additions.label: cor:arith-window-period
additions.topic: Common sufficient period of the reduced inverse and standard-window packets
additions.hypotheses: p prime, m>0, m divides p-1, j<p, n>=1, u natural. Oddness of p is not required.
additions.mathematics: h=(p-1)/m; reduced C_m(n+u*h)=reduced C_m(n), and C_(m*p,j)(n+u*h)=C_(m*p,j)(n) modulo p. h is sufficient, not claimed least.
additions.proof_in_manuscript: Apply the retained all-address theorem at order one; m*n>=1 and v_p(j!)=0; identify reductions using the restored Lucas proposition. The archived Lean proof establishes the same claim directly by the characteristic-p Hurwitz inverse.
